name: Nativism
summary: A political stance that favours established inhabitants over immigrants and holds that a state should belong to its native group. In Cas Mudde's definition it is a xenophobic form of nationalism that treats non-native people and ideas as a threat, and its modern form stresses protecting cultural heritage, reserving jobs and welfare for citizens and requiring assimilation.
scope: Two linked strands: the American nativism of the 1840s-50s (the Know Nothings and the American Party, with their 1856 platform) and the modern European and American nativism that Mudde and Betz describe as the core of the populist radical right. It does not cover the broader populist or authoritarian package beyond what sources tie to nativism, so most answers outside immigration, culture, citizenship and welfare are low-confidence inferences or neutral.

more-religion-public.rationale: Know Nothings centred on Protestant identity and modern nativists redefine the 'us' in Christian terms, but strands differ.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Cultural conservatism on gender is common in the right-wing populist family, but it is not central to nativism.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Betz's symbolic facet: defending the cultural heritage of the native population is central.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Opposition to immigration is the definition of nativism.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Non-native ideas and institutions are seen as threats to a state belonging to its natives.

free-trade.rationale: Right-wing populism is linked to protectionism, but nativism proper is mainly about people not goods.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Right-wing populism is sometimes anti-environmentalist, though an overpopulation-based environmental nativism exists.

revolution-justified.rationale: The platform stressed the Constitution and Union.

experts-over-public.rationale: Elites and academics are portrayed as acting against the people.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Protectionism is associated with the wider family and with jobs reserved for citizens, but it is not core.

one-party-rule.rationale: The Know Nothings ran as a party within electoral politics; modern nativists work in multiparty systems.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The American Party was republican; other strands are indifferent.

direct-votes.rationale: National populists favour a direct conception of democracy over the liberal one.

right-to-secede.rationale: The platform stressed preserving the Union.

political-violence-never.rationale: Nativist movements have included riots and violence, but mainstream adherents disavow it.

separate-church-state.rationale: The 1856 platform opposed any union of church and state, yet Know Nothings also imposed Protestant Bible reading; modern strands differ.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The platform opposed religious tests and church-state union, though it favoured Protestant culture.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Mudde defines nativism as the view that states should be inhabited exclusively by the native group, which may be defined by ethnicity, culture or religion. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Nativism sees the divide as natives against outsiders, not class conflict.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: In the US sense 'native' means the founding settler population, not indigenous peoples, so adherents give them no special authority.

restore-past-order.rationale: Nativism defends an inherited national culture seen as under threat.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Nativism blames outsiders and elites, not profit as such.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Nativists want to restrict exit and entry in the name of the nation.

media-academia-power.rationale: Mudde reports academics, artists and journalists being labelled 'anti-national' elites.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Mudde says nativism may be racist or non-racist, so adherents split.

organic-representation.rationale: The platform relied on ordinary party and electoral politics.

total-state.rationale: The platform stressed constitutional limits and states' reserved rights.

national-rebirth.rationale: Some strands describe cultural decline caused by immigration, but not all.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Nativism seeks to keep the existing state for its natives, not expand it.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: The platform required loyalty to the national constitution, not personal oaths to lords.

bound-labor.rationale: Not part of nativism and at odds with its republican platform.

national-self-determination.rationale: A state for its native nation is the core aim.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Betz's welfare facet: citizens first for benefits.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Defending cultural heritage is the symbolic core of nativism.

workers-nation.rationale: Betz's economic facet reserves jobs for citizens; unions historically backed exclusion.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Mudde says non-natives must assimilate or be repatriated.

elite-replacement.rationale: Mudde documents nativist claims that progressive politicians organise mass immigration, though the explicit replacement framing is not universal. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Mudde reports mainstream and economic elites cast as corrupt and acting against the people.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenic arguments joined some historical nativism (Madison Grant) but are not core.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Nativists want an active state controlling borders and citizenship.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Racial purity arguments appear in some historical strands, but not in cultural nativism.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Newcomers are expected to conform to a single national legal and cultural order.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Know Nothings in Massachusetts required Protestant Bible reading in schools.

population-transfer.rationale: Mudde reports that those who will not assimilate are to be expelled.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Cultural nativism holds that immigrant groups may weaken national identity and cohesion.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: The platform favoured filling offices with native-born citizens, not by lot.

party-controls-media.rationale: Not part of nativism and at odds with its platform.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: The 1856 American Party platform demanded 21 years of residence for citizenship, and nativists have repeatedly sought longer waits.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Nativism does not address officials' pay; populist radical right adherents are split, so this is neutral.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Modern nativist and populist radical right parties oppose the EU and shared sovereignty, defending the nation-state for its native group.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Nativism prizes loyalty to the native nation and treats putting others first as betrayal; defeatism runs against it.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Nativism has no stated position on term limits; the Know Nothings and modern parties differ.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Nativists focus on keeping their own state native, not on reunifying divided nations; adherents are indifferent.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Mudde's definition treats non-native people and ideas as a threat and stresses protecting the native culture, which rejects strict cultural equality.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Nativism does not address school science teaching and adherents are split, with American nativists mainly Protestant.

religious-exemptions.rationale: The 1856 American Party platform targeted Catholics, and nativism treats minority practices as a threat to native culture.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Nativist politics puts its own people first and reserves resources for native citizens, so foreign aid is not owed.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Nativism does not address this; right-wing populists favour popular voice but nativists as such are split.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental risk is not a nativist concern; adherents are indifferent.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The Know Nothings were anti-Catholic and sought to curb church power, but modern nativism is largely secular on this; strands are split.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Nativism has no income-tax doctrine; adherents are split.

character-from-environment.rationale: Nativists demand assimilation, which assumes environment shapes people, yet also treat immigrants as unassimilable by nature; adherents are split.

space-expansion.rationale: Space expansion is not a nativist concern; adherents are indifferent.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Nativism does not address constitutional design; adherents are split.

equal-parenting.rationale: Nativism does not address custody law; adherents are split.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Punishing apostasy is not part of the nativist platform; the 1856 platform opposed church interference in the state.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Mudde describes nativism as requiring assimilation to the native culture.

ban-cartels.rationale: Populist-right parties are split on anti-trust, criticising big business yet backing national firms.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Some nativist parties pair their programme with protectionism, but a country-and-colonies bloc shut off from trade is not part of nativism as Mudde defines it, and the scope excludes the wider populist package.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Adherents are split: protectionists dislike trade deals but oppose externally imposed standards.

delink-world-market.rationale: Nativism does not address this directly; protectionism is common but about the nativists' own economy.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Nativism does not address private-sector discrimination as such; adherents are split.

native-born-offices.rationale: The 1856 American Party platform demanded that offices be filled by native-born citizens.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Nativism does not address divorce; adherents are split.

single-official-language.rationale: Mudde and Betz describe a demand for assimilation into the native culture and language.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Nativism does not address consumption; adherents are split.

job-guarantee.rationale: Nativists want jobs for natives but not necessarily a state guarantee; adherents split.

industrial-unions.rationale: Nativism does not address union structure; adherents split.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Know Nothings feared a Catholic plot against the republic, and modern nativists allege elite plots; the strands vary.

religious-nation.rationale: The Know Nothings were Protestant-centred, while modern nativism is mostly cultural; the strands differ.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Nativism does not address regional revenue; adherents are indifferent or split.

defeat-communism.rationale: Modern nativists tend to be anti-communist but the Know Nothing strand predates communism; adherents are split.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Nativism does not address how services are delivered; adherents are split.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Nativism does not address capitalism's historic role; adherents are split.

majority-settlement.rationale: Nativists favour assimilation but sources show no settlement programme; adherents are split.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Nativism is silent on the capitalism and communism question; adherents are split.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Nativism does not address this; modern radical-right nativists are split and mainly seek to restrict immigration.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Know Nothings were anti-Catholic but did not seek blasphemy laws, and modern nativists do not address it; split.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Populist radical-right nativism claims to speak for the people, but this participatory model is not specific to it; split.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Right-wing populists often claim to transcend left and right, but nativism itself does not address this; split.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Mudde describes modern nativism as treating non-native ideas as a threat; fears of Islam are prominent in the modern European strand. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Nativism does not address this; adherents are split between secular and Christian-heritage views.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Nativism does not address credit institutions; adherents are indifferent or split.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Populist anti-elite rhetoric exists, but nativism does not address press ownership; split.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Anti-Catholic nativism did not typically seek marriage laws, and modern nativists are mostly secular; split.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Boycotts of immigrant-owned shops are a fringe tactic; mainstream adherents are split.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Nativism is indifferent to doctrinal reform; adherents range from defending inherited Christian heritage to secular cultural nativism.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Nativism does not address wealth concentration as such; adherents are split between populist anti-elite and pro-business positions.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Radical-right parties are divided on this; the sources tie nativism to immigration and culture, not to military policy, so this is left neutral.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Nativism favours established inhabitants over immigrants and reserves rights for citizens.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Adherents of the populist radical right are split on foreign bases.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: American nativism had anti-Catholic strands, but the modern form is secular; adherents are split.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Nativism holds that a state should belong to its native group, with jobs reserved for citizens.

independent-unions.rationale: Nativism does not address unions; adherents are split or indifferent.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Nativism does not address the nature of socialism; adherents are split or indifferent.

second-chamber.rationale: Nativism does not address legislative structure; adherents are split or indifferent.

municipal-property.rationale: Nativism does not address ownership of production; adherents are split or indifferent.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Nativism does not address confederal government; adherents are split or indifferent.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Nativism does not address payment privacy; adherents are indifferent or split.

online-anonymity.rationale: Nativism does not address online anonymity; adherents are indifferent or split.

person-over-state.rationale: Nativism puts the native nation first but does not rule on the person against the state; adherents are split.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Nativism sees culture and heritage as central but does not take a stand on a human spiritual nature; the Know Nothings were anti-Catholic, other strands differ.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Nativism does not address regional self-government; adherents are split or indifferent.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Nativism organises around the native group, defined by nation or culture and in the 1850s by religion, not by race as such; adherents are split.

racial-pride.rationale: Nativists value pride in native heritage, but the statement concerns race or ancestry, and strands define the native group culturally rather than racially; split.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Nativism does not address when force is justified; adherents are split or indifferent.

communal-electorates.rationale: Demands assimilation and opposes separate communities; the American Party opposed foreign religious influence.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Nativism does not address labour bargaining; adherents are split between pro-worker and pro-business positions.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Nativism does not address this; welfare is favoured for citizens (s1) but not specifically wage top-ups.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Nativism does not address fiscal rules; adherents are split.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Nativism does not address economic systems; adherents are indifferent or split.

sacred-nation.rationale: Nativism is a form of nationalism that treats the nation as an enduring community to be protected from outsiders (s1, s3). None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Nativism does not address student debt; adherents are split.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Nativism stresses group membership and does not address a universal human nature; adherents are split.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Nativism does not address regional language naming; adherents are indifferent or split.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Nativism does not address how pollution is regulated; adherents are split.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Some nativists back eco-nationalism and others oppose environmental limits; adherents are split.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Mudde describes modern nativism as demanding assimilation to the native culture, and language is its central marker.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Nativism does not address union membership; adherents are indifferent or split.

voter-id.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its rationale rests on proof of citizenship, documents at registration or postal-ballot rules, and the statement now asks only whether voters should show photo ID at polling stations.

reviewHistory.rationale: Preferring native citizens over immigrants and restricting citizenship makes proof of citizenship at the ballot box a natural, commonly stated nativist aim. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

premarital-sex.rationale: Nativism does not address sexual morality; adherents are split between traditionalists and others.

indirect-election.rationale: Nativism does not address how offices are filled; adherents are split.

national-church-status.rationale: The 1856 American Party platform stressed church-state separation and opposed foreign church influence rather than favouring a national church; adherents are split.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Nativism holds the state should belong to the native group and demands assimilation, so ethnic autonomy is rejected.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Nativism does not address disputed territories; adherents are split.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Modern nativist populism criticises elites and parties, yet American nativists organised a party; adherents are split.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: The Know Nothings organised politics around Protestantism against Catholic immigrants, as the 1856 platform shows.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Nothing in the sources addresses automation; the modern nativist emphasis on protecting native jobs cuts both ways.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Nativism's sources do not engage Marxian value theory; it is a nationalist rather than a socialist stance and inclines to market economics.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Mudde and Betz describe protecting native workers' jobs and welfare as central, but nativists mainly stress nation over class, so the fit is partial.

police-more-powers.rationale: Law-and-order authoritarianism is part of the fuller populist-radical-right package built on nativism; unemployment and crime are treated as security problems. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference. (Moved from empower-police-military, 2026-11-11, when that statement became about military spending alone.)

missingStatements.text: Immigrants should have to live in a country for many years before they can become citizens.
missingStatements.rationale: The 1856 American Party platform demanded 21 years of residence for citizenship, and nativists have repeatedly sought longer naturalization waits.

notes: Whether the 'native' group is defined by ethnicity, culture or religion varies by strand and period, and adherents differ on race. The 1850s Know Nothings were anti-Catholic and also mixed on slavery, temperance and labour issues that modern nativists do not share.
